To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyanamide behaves like a vibrational hybrid of the nitriles and isonitriles in its vibrational properties, which is attributed to the strong n → π* conjugation between the N atom and the CN group in the cyanamide group.
cyanamide has vibrational properties intermediate between those of nitrile, isonitrile, and azido groups.
cyanamide is a strongly IR-absorbing reporter that is similar to niterile in vibrational properties and to isonitriles in transition dipole strengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of infrared (IR) reporters that are based on cyanamide.
the synthesis, vibrational properties, and applications of IR probes based on cyanamide, a novel IR reporter.
the development of cyanamide as a new IR probe for the conformational structure and dynamics of proteins and nucleic acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyanamide is an IR reporter with the potential to be stronger and more sensitive to its environment than nitrile but not as strong and as sensitive to the environment as isonitrile.

cyanamide has a vibrational signature that is intermediate between nitrile and the isonitriles, with respect to the three properties of vibrational frequency, transition dipole strength, and vibrational lifetime.
cyanamide is a vibrational hybrid of the nitriles and isonitriles, and it has a potential to be a useful IR reporter of the structure and dynamics of proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CN stretch of cyanamide is a good reporter group for the structural and dynamic studies of biomolecules.

the vibrational properties (vibrational frequency, transition dipole strength, and lifetime) of the CN stretch in the NHCN, CN, NC, and N3 groups are strongly affected by the nature and strength of the n → π interaction between the n and π* orbitals of these groups.
cyanamide is a strong IR reporter with a vibrational frequency and time comparable to nitrile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyanamide is a good IR reporter of conformational structure and dynamics of proteins and other biomolecules.
the vibrational properties and the potential of the NHCX group (X = N, C, and O) as IR probes can be tuned by the electronic and steric effects of the X atom and the substituent groups on the N atom.
cyanamide can be used as a vibrational reporter in IR pump-probe studies to monitor the structural dynamics and conformational changes of biomolecules.
